rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes the joined لكيلا from لكي لا: من بعد علم means immediately after knowledge, while بعد علم can allow a time gap; the spelling reflects that temporal distinction.
rows.anchor: فلمّا احتمل الفاصل فصل (لكي لا) وعندما وصل بينهما وصل (لكيلا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because الدابة usually denotes non-rational creatures and is broad in scope, the wording ما in 16:49 suits both its generality and its usual referents.
rows.anchor: الدابة أغلب ما تستعمل في اللغة لغير العاقل وهي عامة وشاملة فاستعمل (ما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the Qur’an consistently coordinates non-rational beings after من and rational beings after ما; this pattern brings the groups together.
rows.anchor: أما عندما يستعمل (ما) فإنه يعطف عليها ما يعقل (ولله يسجد.. دابة والملائكة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who aids the wronged, directs night and day, and hears and sees all is rightly called the Most High, the Great.
rows.anchor: الناصِر لمن بُغيَ عليه والذي يولج الليل والنهار والسميع البصير أليس هو العلي الكبير؟ بلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Laṭīf is the benefactor who gently delivers benefits; making the earth green after rain is kindness to all creatures.
rows.anchor: لطيف أي متفضِّل على العباد يلطف بهم بإيصال منافعهم أن تصبح الأرض مخضرة هذا من لطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khabīr knows subtle matters and people’s interests, so His gentle care proceeds with knowledge of due measures and wisdom.
rows.anchor: خبير أي عليم بدقائق الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God owns all in the heavens and earth, He is utterly rich; al-Ḥamīd means praised in His wealth and in everything, unlike people who may change when wealthy.
rows.anchor: الحميد هو المحمود في غِناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s subjection of earthly things and restraint of the sky from falling are acts of compassion and mercy, making the closing attributes apt.
rows.anchor: لو لم يرأف بهم ما أمسك السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Sajdah uses هو because its ending mentions their dispute, a context inviting decisive separation; al-Ḥajj ends by calling God witness and omits هو.
rows.anchor: لأن خاتمة آية سورة السجدة (فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic and Arabic fronting does not always signal greater merit: mosques are best in this list, yet the context warrants listing them last; Moses and Aaron also change order by context.
rows.anchor: هي أفضل المذكور في الآية لكن أحياناً يُقدّم ما هو أقل تفضيلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis depends on context: al-Mu’minūn mentions death more often and foregrounds human creation, so creation receives two emphases and resurrection one, since resurrection is easier than originating life; both are easy for God.
rows.anchor: فلهذا جعل سبحانه وتعالى توكيدين في الخلق وتوكيداً واحداً في البعث لأن البعث أهون عليه من الخلق من عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people forget death and act as if immortal, he cites the hadith urging remembrance of it; the verse is not addressing resurrection-deniers, and human attempts at worldly immortality fail.
rows.anchor: لتُوهّم أن الإنسان قد يكون مخلّداً في الدنيا لكن الحقيقة أن الإنسان سيموت وكثيراً ما يغفل الإنسان عن الموت وينساق وراء شهواته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Naḥl, deletion of the nūn in تك conveys removing every trace of distress as consolation; al-Naml’s non-consolatory context uses the complete تكن.
rows.anchor: فحذفت النون من الفعل. أما في آية سورة النمل

words: أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِّن مَّنِيٍّ يُمْنَى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn is omitted in يك because the sperm is still incomplete and unfertilized, matching the incomplete state and unfinished event.
rows.anchor: حذفت النون هنا لأن النطفة هي من الذكر وهي غير مكتملة بعد وغير مخصّبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the Qur’anic account of embryonic stages matches knowledge reached only in the modern era, which specialists in anatomy and medicine describe as scientifically precise.
rows.anchor: مما لم يكن معروفاً قبل هذا العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term ʿalaqah is apt because the developing creature at that stage most resembles the known parasitic leech.
rows.anchor: المخلوق في هذه المرحلة أشبه شيء بالعلقة وهي الطفيلية المعروفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muḍghah is chewed flesh; he says modern science shows the embryo at this stage resembles meat chewed by teeth, making the term more precise than a generic small piece of flesh.
rows.anchor: أن الجنين في هذه المرحلة ليس قطعة لحم عادية بل هو كقطعة اللحم التي مضغتها الأسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He claims modern historical and archaeological discoveries about Dhul-Qarnayn align word for word with the Qur’an and were unknown to earlier exegetes.
rows.anchor: وما توصلوا إليه في هذا القرن منطبق على ما جاء في القرآن الكريم كلمةً كلمة ولم يكن ذلك معلوماً قبل هذا القرن

words: فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
rows.speaker: كتب التفسير
rows.claim: According to the tafsir books, the Day of Resurrection lasts fifty thousand years, but it is eased for the believer to the length of an obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: مقدار يوم القيامة كما في الآية هو خمسين ألف سنة حسب ما جاء في كتب التفسير وهذا اليوم يُخفف على المؤمن

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes interpret the heart as the intellect.
rows.anchor: القلب عند بعض المفسرين هو العقل

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Another group says the heart is not the intellect, citing the verse about hearts in the chests being blind.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال ليس العقل بدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is an unseen spiritual faculty, not the chest’s physical organ; reason can judge without acting, while the heart moves a person to act on belief and is therefore more important.
rows.anchor: ليس المقصود بالقلب المضغة الموجودة في الصدر إنما المقصود أمر آخر أمر روحي بدليل أن القلب هو أمر روحاني غيبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative من is singular in form but may denote singular, dual, or plural; Arabic commonly observes its singular form first and then its plural sense.
rows.anchor: في كلام العرب يراعى المفرد أولاً ثم الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes presence or witnessing (حضور) from coming, which is movement between places; Qur’anic examples use both for death and for arriving events.
rows.anchor: أما المجيء فهو الإنتقال من مكان إلى مكان، فالحضور إذن غير المجيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes God as present everywhere and presents this as evidence of His existence everywhere.
rows.anchor: ولهذا نقول الله حاضر في كل مكان دليل وجوده في كل مكان

none: Qur’an quotations only; the excerpt breaks off mid-quote.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isra is a night journey; the wording ليلاً rather than الليل indicates that the journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and ascent took only part of the night.
rows.anchor: وقد جاءت كلمة (ليلاً) بدل الليل لأن الليل تدل على الليل كله أما الإسراء فقد تم في جزء من الليل فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the Sacred Mosque indicates that no harm can occur there, and the phrase may mean the precise location from which the journey began.
rows.anchor: أي من عين المكان ويكفي تسمية المسجد الحرام يعني أن لا يحدث فيه سوء

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars say the Night Journey began at Umm Hani’s house rather than at the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: أكثر العلماء يقولون أن الإسراء لم يتم من المسجد الحرام وإنما من بيت أم هانئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the designation as an indication that all of Mecca is a sanctuary, even if the journey began at Umm Hani’s house.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التفاتة إلى أن مكة كلها حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although it was not yet a mosque at the time, calling it the Farthest Mosque signals that it would become one.
rows.anchor: لم يكن آنذاك مسجداً لكن هذا إشارة إلى أنه سيكون مسجداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying God blessed its surroundings both honors the mosque and gives the blessing broad scope, including spiritual and material good, provision, and messengers rather than a fixed set of objects.
rows.anchor: أما باركنا حوله فهو يشمل كل ما حوله وهو تعظيم للمسجد نفسه ولكنه إشارة أن المباركة حول المسجد أيضاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third person in سبحان الذي أسرى to God’s first-person لنريه identifies God as the direct speaker; the purposive wording also signals a planned journey with wisdom, whether disclosed or hidden.
rows.anchor: إلتفات لأسلوب المتكلم بعد أن ابتدأ بالغائب (سبحان الذي أسرى) إلتفت سبحانه للمتكلم ليدلّ على أن المتكلّم هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prompted by a reader’s observation that Moses’ narratives in al-Naml and al-Qaṣaṣ closely resemble one another, he set out to explain their wording differences, including these paired expressions.
rows.anchor: من نحو قوله تعالى: "فلما جاءها نودي" و "فلما أتاها نودي"
